name: Holden Commodore
overview: The Holden Commodore was Australia's definitive full-size passenger car, holding the crown as the nation's best-selling car for 15 consecutive years (1996-2010). Spanning 16 distinct series codes across five generations from the original 1978 VB to the billion-dollar Australian-engineered VE/VF Zeta platform and the imported European ZB, the Commodore was the family hauler, police highway patrol interceptor, commercial utility, and Mount Panorama Bathurst racing champion for over four decades.
australian_market_notes: First conceived in response to the 1973 oil crisis as a smaller, more fuel-efficient alternative to the full-size Kingswood, Holden heavily re-engineered the German Opel Rekord/Senator body with 35% heavier structural reinforcement, MacPherson strut front suspension, four-trailing-arm rear suspension, and Holden's own Red, Blue, and Black sixes and V8s. In 1986, the VL adopted the high-revving Nissan RB30 3.0L straight-six and legendary Turbo option. The 1988 VN introduced a widened body tailored specifically to Australian shoulder-room expectations and the rugged Buick-sourced 3.8L V6. The 2006 VE marked a monumental $1.03 billion investment creating the global GM Zeta rear-wheel-drive platform in Melbourne and Adelaide. The final Australian-built Commodore—a Red Hot VF II SS-V Redline sedan—rolled off the Elizabeth line on 20 October 2017.
